name: add_kotlin_cache_ttl_expiry
description: Add TTL-based expiry to a plain key-value Cache, with an injectable Clock for deterministic testing; broken uses an exclusive expiry boundary so an entry exactly at its expiry instant is served one extra tick
prompts: Cache<K, V> in Cache.kt is a plain unbounded key-value store with no expiry. Add TIME-TO-LIVE support: put(key, value, ttlMillis: Long? = null) - null (or omitted) means the entry never expires - and get(key) returns null once an entry has expired, WITHOUT using real wall-clock sleeps in this task (that would make tests slow/flaky). Instead introduce a small `Clock` abstraction (a functional interface with a `now(): Long` method) that Cache takes as a constructor parameter, defaulting to System.currentTimeMillis() so existing callers are unaffected, but swappable in tests. An entry is expired AT its exact expiry instant (clock.now() >= expiresAt), not just strictly after it, and once get() observes an expired entry it must actually remove it from the store (so size() reflects reality). Keep put/get/size's basic behavior for non-expiring entries unchanged.
